content.title: Color, Contrast, and More Than Color
content.hook: Color can help people scan a page, but color should not be the only way important information is communicated. A red message that means “error” is weaker if red is the only clue.
content.context: Color can help people scan a page, but color should not be the only way important information is communicated. A red message that means “error” is weaker if red is the only clue.
goals: Use color as support rather than the only carrier of meaning and recognize why text and controls need sufficient contrast.

interactive.caption: Verify WCAG 2.1 AA/AAA luminance contrast and typographic clarity for accessible interface design.

content.question: A dashboard marks errors only with red text. What is the better design?

options.text: Add another meaningful cue such as an icon, text, or clear status label.

feedback.correct: Important meaning should remain available without depending on color alone.
feedback.incorrect: Important meaning should remain available without depending on color alone.

content.title: Contrast as a reading question
content.text: Text needs enough contrast against its background to remain readable. Contrast is not a “nice-looking palette” problem. It is a perception problem.

content.question: A designer puts light gray body text on a white background because it looks subtle. What should you ask first?

options.text: Whether the text remains sufficiently distinct from the background for people to read.
Whether the CSS file is named correctly.
Whether the button can open another page.
Whether the paragraph contains exactly 20 words.

feedback.correct: Readability comes before subtle visual styling. Contrast is part of whether users can perceive the content.
feedback.incorrect: Readability comes before subtle visual styling. Contrast is part of whether users can perceive the content.

content.title: States must also be clear
content.text: Interactive controls have states such as normal, focused, selected, disabled, or error. Those states should not become indistinguishable when color changes are ignored.

content.title: State with more than color
content.text:
```html

Error: Enter a valid email address.

```

content.question: Why is the text in the status example useful?

options.text: It communicates the error without requiring the user to interpret a color.
It guarantees every user will agree on the design.

feedback.correct: The words carry the meaning. Color can reinforce the message, but the meaning survives without it.
feedback.incorrect: The words carry the meaning. Color can reinforce the message, but the meaning survives without it.
